title: One error format for a whole API
problem: chats_api.py is finished: it raises an AppError, raises HTTPException (sometimes with headers), and has validated bodies and paths. Its errors still come out in FastAPI's default formats. Write install_error_handlers(app) in errors.py so that every error response uses one envelope, keeps its headers, follows the course's 400/422 policy and never echoes the request input.
requirements: Every error body is {"error": {"code": str, "message": str}}; validation errors add "fields"
AppError: its own status, code and message
Any Starlette/FastAPI HTTPException (yours, and the router's 404/405): its status; code from STATUS_CODES, or "http_error" for other statuses; message = str(detail); the exception's headers are kept
RequestValidationError with any error of type json_invalid: 400, code "malformed_json", message "request body is not valid JSON", no fields
Other RequestValidationError: 422, code "validation_failed", message "request validation failed", fields = one {"loc": loc joined with ".", "type": type, "message": msg} per error, in order
No error response contains the request's input values
contract: install_error_handlers(app: FastAPI) -> None   # registers exception handlers on app
expectedBehavior: GET /chats/5 -> 404 {"error": {"code": "chat_not_found", "message": "chat 5 not found"}}; PUT /chats -> 405 with Allow: POST; POST /chats {"title": ""} -> 422 with fields [{"loc": "body.title", "type": "string_too_short", ...}]; broken JSON -> 400 malformed_json
edgeCases: The router's own 404 and 405 must use the format too
405 must keep Allow; 401 must keep WWW-Authenticate
A status not in STATUS_CODES (418) gets code http_error
A field_validator's ValueError must not crash the handler
Path errors have locs like path.chat_id
hints: Conceptual: three exception classes reach your handlers: AppError, Starlette's HTTPException and RequestValidationError. Each needs one handler, and all three should build the body the same way.

Specific: register handlers inside install_error_handlers (decorators on app, or app.add_exception_handler(cls, func)). Pass headers=exc.headers for HTTP errors. In the validation handler, check for type "json_invalid" first, then build fields from loc, type and msg only.

Implementation: write a helper error_response(status, code, message, headers=None, **extra) that returns JSONResponse(status_code=status, content={"error": {"code": code, "message": message, **extra}}, headers=headers), and call it from each handler. Join locs with ".".join(str(p) for p in err["loc"]).
evaluation: The envelope is built in one place
HTTP handler is registered for Starlette's HTTPException and keeps headers
Validation fields are rebuilt from loc/type/msg; input and ctx never reach the response
